Its three surfaces - Authoring, VRChat - no camera depth, VRChat - camera depth available - are no longer available and nothing replaces them. The menu path did not move, so there is nothing to look for. To check whether depth is actually being supplied, set Depth Sampling > Depth Availability to Diagnostic in the material inspector; it paints the detection state on screen.

The colour and intensity of additional lights - point and spot - are added thinly into the Fresnel rim. Until now the rim answered the main light alone, so a silhouette edge stayed the main light's colour even in a scene lit from the side by a coloured lamp. A material with Enable Fresnel Rim on gets a different edge colour in a scene with additional lights. How much is added is bound to Rim Light's colour and Blend Opacity, so several lights together still do not blow out to white. Nothing is added on a material with Enable Fresnel Rim off or Intensity at 0, and the whole thing drops out in Performance Distance's far band. It reads no extra texture. On URP the Fresnel rim used to take additional lights twice; it now matches BRP. Both backends multiply by the main light and add the additional ones, one way only. A URP material gets a different rim colour in a scene with additional lights.
documents.s: Point and spot lights now reach Rim Light

documents.t: The value stored in the bundled presets came down from 10 to 1. When the purity ceiling was widened to 0-10 the preset values were saved pinned to that ceiling, so applying a factory look pushed the rim colour into oversaturation. 1 means the composed colour as-is, the same as the shader default. It takes effect only when you apply a preset again. A value already stored on a material you made is left alone.
documents.s: The factory looks' Rim Light > Color Purity default is now 1

documents.t: Applying a Look Preset, saving a preset and applying a JSON document all work regardless of the version stored on the material. Those three paths used to refuse an older material with an error telling you to run the project migration first. That check, the error and the dialog that offered to run the migration are all gone. The official path from 0.1.6 is to delete the Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon folder and import 0.1.7 fresh. So many property names changed that old values do not carry over, so dial your materials back in from the new defaults and use a Look Preset if you want to get there faster. Bake output has to be baked again too. Nothing in the product requires the migration any more. Improvements
documents.s: A material's version no longer blocks presets and JSON

documents.t: The more MatCap layers a material stacks, the bigger the difference. You can see it on the Performance Cost meter once you rebake. Materials that do not use MatCap are unchanged. Materials you upload to VRChat and WARUDO now cost the same as they do on URP. Until now an identically configured material was heavier on the Built-in side alone.
documents.s: 10. Avatars that use MatCap get lighter

documents.t: The workspace bar has five tabs. Optimize contains texture optimization and per-type resolution caps; automatic build and play-mode hooks are configured in Upload. Analyze in Optimize produces four suggestions for this avatar: bake materials with identical settings as one, fold uniform textures into constants, pack mask textures together, and switch off modules that have no effect. All are off by default. Choices are remembered per avatar in this computer's user settings. Expand the material selection tools below the workspace bar to use All, Face, Face & Skin, Common and Exclude Face. Overview starts with the current avatar state and next action. Expand the estimated-spec card to see material slots, estimated draw calls (authoring and baked), the highest texture-binding count, the highest per-pixel depth read count, texture memory and the VRChat performance rank those imply. These are estimates; the SDK build panel remains the source of the final numbers. The same screen toggles Depth Effects, 2D Shadow, Enable SSAO, Cast Shadow and Outline across the whole avatar at once, with undo.
documents.s: An Optimize tab, an estimated-spec card and a material selection row in the Manager

documents.t: Transparent Draw Order was added to 3 · Details on the Manager's Look & Bake tab. Transparent parts are drawn in order of distance from the camera, but an avatar's skinned meshes usually share one large bounds, so every part reports the same distance. Sorting Order alone then decides, and parts left on the same value are tied — which is how a ribbon ends up behind the blouse it belongs on top of. Find Parts With Undecided Order collects the groups distance cannot separate, listed per shared material. Order them yourself with ▲▼ in the list; up is behind, down is in front. Left unordered, Unity picks between them arbitrarily, and the choice can change every time the scene is reopened or the avatar is built.
documents.s: Transparent Draw Order in the Manager

documents.t: Matcap layers that only add and carry no mask are merged into a single map at bake time; the layer count and its keyword come down with them. A texture slot that is empty, or whose texels are all one colour, folds into a constant - the sample and the binding disappear together. A material with outlines authored off no longer submits the outline hull pass, as long as nothing animates its outline properties. That is one pass fewer per slot. Depth Effect Mask and Outline Width Mask join the existing mask pack, two textures fewer. All of it needs a rebake to apply.
documents.s: The bake removes more textures and draw calls

documents.t: Simple was reorganised into 6 groups and 22 sections. Form Shadow, Normal Outline, Face Shading, Depth Effects - Common, Inner 2D Edge and SSAO moved into Simple; Master Adjust, Stencil and Glitter moved out to Full. Simple keeps every section and shows only the values that actually get adjusted. Face Border now displays on the same normalized 0-1 scale as the body border and is mirrored into the Form Shadow tab for face materials. Edge Rim Minimum Multiplier was added to Master Adjust; a material seen for the first time opens only Quick Settings and leaves the other sections collapsed. 2D Shadow Bias was also capped from 10 to 1. The ? button on a section header opens the matching page of the online documentation in the inspector's language. 33 sections map onto 22 pages, and the Manager and the Validator warnings link the same way. Property tooltips were expanded considerably. The share of inspector-visible shader properties carrying a tooltip went from 30.7% to 41.8% (160 more), all three languages filled in. The Manager has five tabs: Overview, Setup, Look & Bake, Upload and Optimize. Overview shows current status and the actual next action; Setup owns conversion inputs; Look & Bake reapplies the look after conversion and rebakes while preserving selected scope and options; Upload runs the normal automatic path, checks the current avatar, then exposes advanced manual bake; Optimize owns project optimization without a duplicate automatic-hook instruction. Section headers went from 34 to 22 points tall and the gap between sections narrowed. The master toggle is a checkbox instead of a pill whose width moved with its label, and the ?, favourite and reset icons line up across every section. Collapse All and Expand All are in the inspector's top bar and in the pinned bar both. Collapsing leaves the workflow group banners open, so the list of closed tabs reads at a glance. The pinned bar gained a Changed Only view, the cost grade with the module driving it, workflow group jump buttons, and a row naming the section you are currently inside (clicking it collapses that section). The bug that stopped the bar following the scroll at 200% scaling is fixed too.
documents.s: The inspector and the Manager, tidied

documents.t: VRC Light Volumes (Test) is an in-editor preview toggle. A VRChat avatar upload turns the module on regardless of the value, reading the Light Volumes the world placed instead of Unity light probes, and the value stored on the material is restored once the upload finishes. In a world without volumes it falls back to probes and the picture is unchanged. A world build turns it on only when the scene actually holds a Light Volume component. Turning it on in the editor compiles one more variant and adds a Texture3D read, so enable it only to preview the look in a volume world. Built-in only; the row does not appear on a URP material.
documents.s: VRC Light Volumes turn on automatically for an upload

documents.t: Development console logs are stripped from the C# sources that go into the package. 27 lines - shader warm-up progress, internal bake tags and the like - no longer appear. Not one warning or error was removed, and the logs that report the result of something you asked for stay as well.

Switching a baked material's shader back to the editable one by hand leaves the MatCap atlas values behind with no per-layer maps. The MatCap Layers tab now opens with a yellow warning at the top: "This material still carries the bake-only MatCap atlas values, so the MatCap layers look empty. Use the original material, or bake it again." There is no automatic repair, because guessing the maps back would be inventing content. Restore the recorded editable material or bake again. Restore, cleanup, the backend swap and migration all leave a baked copy's shader alone, so no normal path raises this warning.
documents.s: A warning on a material left holding bake-only MatCap values

documents.t: When Performance Distance (m) times Performance Distance Scale is 0, the material renders at its lightest tier at every distance and the camera-depth effects, PBR, the extra matcap and normal layers, toon specular, glitter and screen tone never draw. The validator now reports that as MING-MAT-PERF-DISTANCE-ZERO. It is a warning, not an error. Zero is a legal authored value and the end MLC drives the scale down to in game, so a material parked there on purpose is fine as it is; otherwise the message points you at Performance Distance Scale on the Master Adjust tab.
documents.s: The validator catches a material with a performance distance of zero

documents.t: The bulk edit panel that changes several materials at once gained a Base Map Opacity row. The mask authoring button now supports the blend mask slots on emission layers 1 and 2. Those two were the only slots left off the list. Seven slots the per-type texture resolution caps could not classify - Reflection Color / Mask, Reflection Cubemap, Gradation LUT and the MatCap and emission mask slots - were put in their place. Those textures no longer stay at their source resolution when a cap is set. Outline Master was registered in the module list. The retired properties _DepthShadowDistanceReach, _SsaoQuality and _SsaoFarDistance were missing from the retired list, so the values stored on a material were never cleaned up. Migrate Project To Current Schema now clears them with the rest. That command is optional, and a leftover value does not affect the look.
documents.s: Entries that were missing from a list

documents.t: The install wait now covers only the variants a default scene needs on first paint (the predicted first-paint requests plus the recorded variants that match that lighting) and hands the editor back the moment they land. Everything else keeps compiling behind the Progress window on the same asynchronous job, which is not gated on editor focus. The stall window is longer, so a slow cold first compile is no longer misread as a stall and dropped to the serial compile path. A conversion's prewarm joins the running asynchronous job instead of the focus-gated runner. Conversion skips the mesh bake stage entirely when no mesh channel is checked, and the re-pin/save step shows its own progress text.
documents.s: The post-install / post-conversion warm-up wait ends at the first-paint set

documents.t: Every Face preset now uses Softness 0.001. The three presets with the 2D shadow enabled set Receiver Depth Pushback and Depth Stretch to 0, keep Face 2D Shadow Assist off, and use a 2D Shadow Bias of 0.15. This applies only to presets you apply from now on; existing materials are untouched. Bug fixes
documents.s: 2D shadow values of the factory Face look presets

documents.t: It now moves across smoothly. This affects every material using an SDF face.
documents.s: 11. Face shading snapped hard as the light crossed the centre of the face

documents.t: On a unified material with the face vertex-painted, shadows falling on the body sat away from where they belonged. It now applies to the face only.
documents.s: 12. A depth offset meant for the face alone pushed the body with it

documents.t: You had to restart the editor before you could rebake. It rebakes immediately now.
documents.s: 13. Deleting a bake output and baking again failed

documents.t: Those two rows were missing from the inspector entirely, so unlike the first slot there was no way to pick a channel. Both slots match now.
documents.s: 14. You could not choose Channel Source or Invert Source Colors on the second emission slot

documents.t: Two preset scope toggles were clipped in Korean and Japanese, leaving them unreadable — Overwrite Shadow Colors Too and Overwrite Fresnel Too are now split across two lines. Narrowing the inspector clipped the sliders and number fields in the middle, so you could not type a value — the value column survives at narrow widths now. The revert button sat outside its row's box with too much margin on the right — it now sits inside the box it belongs to.
If you do not read Korean there was no way back to English or Japanese. It follows the system language now.
documents.s: 16. Opening Face SDF Studio first locked the MingToon inspector to Korean as well

documents.t: Even when the proxy centre is placed in front of the face, the target normal now stays within the visible face hemisphere. Removed the separate planar-normal blend called Normal Method. Proxy Normal Intensity is now the only blend between the original and proxy-shaped normals. Proxy radius now controls actual normal curvature. Smaller sphere, cylinder and capsule proxies bend normals more strongly; larger ones transition more gently. The top-left Scene view panel can independently toggle normal lines and the proxy volume, while display length and density remain independent from rendered lighting. Materials using a texture face-region mask now preview normal lines with the actual UV, channel, inversion, and remapping. If the mask cannot be sampled, the tool hides misleading lines and reports why.
documents.s: 17. Face proxy normals flipped under front lighting or reacted over an unnaturally narrow angle

documents.t: The VRChat face-normal bake isolates build-only Face slots with temporary materials. It does not mutate the scene's original Meshes and materials or materials shared by another avatar. For each face-normal optimization build root, it first records the original Mesh and material slots of every Renderer that has a Mesh. Recovery restores even non-Face Renderer Meshes replaced by a later upload conversion, and resumes journal and temporary-material ownership recovery across script reloads or editor restarts. Regular conversion records Renderers, Meshes, materials, Prefab overrides, and dirty state before each mutation. Its journal is written atomically under ProjectSettings; a backup repairs a damaged primary file, and an older Library journal is migrated once. After eight failed automatic recovery attempts, retry from the Advanced menu or inspect the pending work before discarding only the recovery journal.
documents.s: 18. Upload and conversion recovery is now interruption-safe

documents.t: When a build was interrupted and its material was deleted afterwards, the recovery could never complete - yet it retried on every domain reload and printed a fresh red error each time, so it appeared on every script recompile and every entry into Play mode. The first attempt now waits for the import to finish, and only records whose material is gone from the project are dropped, once, with their names. Only after three failed attempts does it name the materials still waiting and what to do about them, in a single warning, and then it stays quiet. A recovery failure during a build or an upload still stops the build as before.
documents.s: Startup recovery is incomplete repeated on every editor start

documents.t: On a pixel where normal layers were stacked inverted and at full strength, the math could overflow and drop the whole normal stack. The same limit in the direction vectors the 2D Shadow and the 2D Rim Light use is fixed with it. Where the tangent is near zero, BRP and URP built different tangent frames, and the 2D Shadow's depth-placement fallback pointed forward on one backend and backward on the other. Both now use the same expression on both. The first two are defensive fixes that only surface on a GPU that really runs half precision; the last two were a BRP/URP result difference that showed on PC as well. Verified through the shader compile gate; not verified in a live render.
documents.s: Four precision and backend-mismatch fixes in the normal and depth math

documents.t: Unticking a region and applying left the slot it had already written in place, so a region applied once could not be removed with the tool. Apply now writes all four slots, and a region left off is actually removed from the material. The window does not read the material's current values. Applying an empty window over a material whose stack, normal or MatCap slots are already filled clears those slots, so set the window's regions up before applying. Undo (Ctrl+Z) works.
documents.s: Regions could not be taken back out in the One Slot / Tiled Regions window

documents.t: The module's shader keyword was declared on neither BRP nor URP, so switching it on applied no ramp and the whole thing dropped out of the compile. It works now. A material that already had Gradation LUT on looks different. The ramp that was ignored until now is applied to the base colour. Switch the row off if you need the old picture. On a material using UV scrolling, rotation or atlas animation, Built-in alone skipped the ramp; that is fixed with it. It needs a rebake to apply.
documents.s: Turning Gradation LUT on did nothing

documents.t: Render Disabled (do not draw this material) now blocks the screen draw and removes depth/shadow passes at the vertex stage on both Built-in and URP. Hidden materials no longer write camera depth or the light shadow map, so they do not cast 2D shadows, SSAO contact, or projected shadows. Older hidden materials are healed on next selection or project migration.
documents.s: Render Disabled could not switch the transparent depth prepass off

documents.t: MingToon > Create Look Preset From Prefab in the Project window wrote every unsaved change in the project to disk at save time. It now saves only the preset asset it actually created or overwrote.
documents.s: Creating a look preset from a prefab saved unrelated work with it

documents.t: The preview read its own temporary material, decided there was no face, and never built the data to draw the normal lines from at all. It now judges from the original material's values.
documents.s: The face proxy Scene view preview was never built

documents.t: The conversion wrote the emission map and mask fresh but left Channel Source, Invert Source Colors and the blend mask's channel and inversion at the pre-conversion material's values, so either emission layer could come out different from the original. The conversion now resets those values with the rest.
documents.s: lilToon conversion left the emission channel settings at their old values

documents.t: A configuration that locked a Photo Look Bit to a fixed value was refused at the install step with a "no target binding" error. Fixed.
documents.s: Ming Light Controller — a configuration with a Photo Look Bit pinned was refused at install

documents.t: If you connect an external or shared Face SDF map while Face SDF Studio has an automatic refresh waiting, it checks the connection again just before applying the older automatic job so that job does not overwrite your map.
documents.s: Preserve a map changed manually while Face SDF auto refresh is pending

documents.t: The cleanup checks every material contained in one asset file and changes it to the current shader. It first checks that the material can be saved, then reads the saved reference again after the change. If it cannot save or verify the result, it leaves the existing generated profile and keeps the cleanup incomplete.
documents.s: Verify material references when cleaning up 0.1.6 generated profiles

documents.t: Turning off automatic camera settings in the Inspector removes the settings that automation applied. When you use an existing post-processing layer, it does not overwrite the layer mask and volume trigger settings you changed later.
documents.s: Disable automatic camera settings without overwriting later settings

documents.t: The shader variant's compilation errors are checked after it is warmed up. A variant with an error is not recorded as ready, and the failure reason is reported.
documents.s: A compile failure was recorded as a completed warmup

documents.t: When the original mask and settings saved in the project match, the same mask pack is reused after reopening the Editor. Existing packs are neither deleted nor renamed, so the first application of this change can create one new pack.
documents.s: Reuse the same mask pack after restarting the Editor

documents.t: The baked profile of a material that uses an alpha mask or a region mask failed to compile on D3D11, so the build hook left that material on the editable shader for the upload. That put every variant of the editable shader into the avatar bundle and made the upload about five minutes longer. Avatars that are already uploaded need a re-upload to receive this fix.
documents.s: Baked shaders of materials with an alpha mask or region mask failed to compile

documents.t: When no mesh channel was checked and the mesh bake was skipped, the conversion itself finished but building the completion dialog title threw a NullReferenceException. Fixed.
documents.s: NullReferenceException in the conversion completion dialog

documents.t: Fixes re-published without a version bump are listed round by round on the 0.1.7 Hotfix page.

0.1.7 hotfix · the package version stays 0.1.7 How to read a hotfix A hotfix is the same 0.1.7 package uploaded again without a version bump. Download it again from BOOTH and overwrite Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon. To see which round your package contains, check the entries in Docs/PATCH_NOTES_0.1.7.md inside the package. New rounds are always added at the top of this page.

After updating The face proxy needs nothing beyond the overwrite. Open the scene and the editable material's proxy normal is computed by the shader right away. No re-upload is needed. A material converted from a lilToon source with no outline that relies on stencil needs a re-conversion or the Outline > Stencil Settings matched to the surface values by hand. A material with Enable Emission on needs a re-conversion or one press of Sync Fallback Properties in the Manager, then a re-upload, before its VRChat fallback turns black. A project whose VRChat build was stuck on Material recovery is incomplete cleans itself up after one editor restart following the overwrite. lilToon-converted materials that rely on stencil (eye overlays, hidden-mesh masks) need a re-conversion or the stencil values set back by hand. No re-upload is needed.

Symptom — a tuned proxy snapped back to the original normals at every scene save, Play mode, reload or validation, and meanwhile the inspector pointed at a preview clone so edits never reached the source material. Fix — the temporary UV7 preview mesh and material swap is gone. On the editable material the shader computes the proxy normal itself. The upload copy is still baked from the proxy settings as before, and that material compiles the live path out. Live and baked use the same math. Also fixed — on a Skinned Mesh Renderer with a Root Bone the Proxy Area Mask center landed off the face. The shader's object space there is the root bone's (usually Hips), so the editor now publishes a per-renderer correction.
documents.s: Face proxy normals kept "coming undone" in the scene

documents.t: Symptom — an eye stencilled to show through the fringe showed through on the surface while its outline stayed hidden behind the hair. lilToon variants without an outline carry unused outline stencil values, and the outline MingToon draws after conversion received that neutral unit. Fix — when the source draws no outline, the outline inherits the surface stencil unit. A source that draws its own outline keeps its own values as before.
documents.s: Converting a lilToon material with no outline left its outline ignoring the stencil mask

documents.t: Symptom — an avatar dropped to the fallback by a shader block or a failed shader load came out white with only its outline left. The fallback _EmissionColor carried the tint × intensity of any material with Enable Emission on, and the VRChat fallback shaders add that colour over the whole surface when no emission map is set. Fix — the fallback emission alias is now always black. MingToon's own emission is unchanged.
documents.s: The VRChat fallback shader painted the whole avatar white with the emission colour

documents.t: Symptom — after one build of an avatar that uses NDMF, every later VRChat build failed with Material recovery is incomplete. Fix — recovery records for the clone materials NDMF creates under Packages/nadena.dev.ndmf/__Generated/ and deletes after the build stayed in the journal. The missing-material check now looks at the file on disk instead of the GUID mapping alone, and such records are cleared at the next recovery with a single warning.
documents.s: Stale NDMF clone records kept blocking the VRChat build

documents.t: Symptom — the lilToon conversion carries the source stencil unit across (Ref, Comp, Pass and so on), but the factory look applied right after it held the shader defaults (Ref 0, Always, Keep), so the stencil that eye overlays and hidden-mesh masks rely on went back to 0. Re-applying a look did the same. Fix — both stencil units (surface and outline, 14 properties) are now neither captured into nor written by a preset.
documents.s: Look presets overwrote the stencil values

documents.t: Open Beta · 2026-09-08
Permanent link: 0.1.8 patch notes

First-upload time — Improved the excessive time required for uploads. User measurements report a 3–50% improvement for a first upload; results vary by environment. White VRC-baked characters — In the VRC bake path, emission layers are now composed sequentially over the current lit result instead of overwriting it, addressing characters turning white after a bake and upload. Emission masks, shadow visibility, Normal/Multiply blending, map RGB/alpha, and surface alpha are retained. Re-bake and re-upload existing baked materials to receive this change. Fallback path distinction — The change that forces the fallback emission alias (_EmissionColor) to black shipped separately in the 0.1.7 HotFix1 release. This 0.1.8 fix covers emission composition in the regular MingToon bake/render path. Re-bake and re-upload baked materials created before 0.1.7 HotFix1. Ming Light Controller 0.1.1 — BRP-only projects no longer fail because a missing URP shader was validated during upload. MLC now validates each installed MingToon backend and reports an error only when neither backend is installed. Authorized transient IDs for NDMF build clones stay in memory and never rewrite the source avatar or project files. The menu's Saturation control binds to MingToon's Output Master Saturation. MLC is a separate package; update it after installing MingToon. Recovery when an older Assets installation conflicts — Only when the older Assets-based installation conflicts with the new installer and installation fails, first move any .mat, texture, or preset files saved directly inside Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon elsewhere, then delete only that MingToon folder and import again. Do not delete MingLightController or the entire StudioRaming folder. This cleanup is needed once when migrating from the older Assets installation and is not repeated for later VPM updates. Conversion stability — Fixed lilToon conversion changing SSAO color purity, disabling emission masks, or changing mask data through compression. Upload texture rewrites (opt-in) — The default LosslessOnly texture bake policy never rewrites authored texels. Enable Reviewed Texture Rewrites On Build (Opt-In) on Optimize only with Optimize On Build / Upload (Applies To Everything) enabled to flatten Texture Layers and Normal Layers before upload and pack loose masks into RGBA. Color-space conversion, regenerated mips, or platform compression can change pixels, so compare target-platform captures before and after baking; the widened pack also includes Width Mask on the Outline tab. Manager controls — Update status and installed/latest versions now fit in two rows at about one third of the previous height, with Check, Update, and Notes in one place. Installation and update paths — Import the DLL unitypackage downloaded from BOOTH to install the required MingToon package automatically without an additional install button. This is the VCC/VPM-based path introduced in this release. Unity then checks for new versions at startup and shows a notice for versions that have neither been installed nor skipped. The user must click the Update button in the notice to install; if Unity is playing, compiling, or building, it waits and checks again after reload. Restarting Unity does not install a version automatically. Skip applies only to that version, and the next new version is announced again. Users who installed through VCC continue to maintain and update it manually through VCC. Existing asset preservation — Existing 0.1.7 installations and inventories are recognized; package updates touch only managed files and preserve existing materials, scenes, prefabs, and Unity-created package.json.meta files.

Color Presets — Use the Color Presets panel to save and apply the full Shadow Color tab (bands, chroma, brightness, and color map), rim/depth tints, and HSVG. The seven factory palettes are Neutral, Warm Tone 1, Warm Tone 2, Cool Tone 1, Cool Tone 2, High Saturation, and Low Saturation. Textures outside the preset's targets, render state, and keywords stay intact; presets apply to multiple selected materials and support Undo. Band and rim color controls — Quick settings expose overall saturation and emission intensity, while SSAO Color, Rim Shade Color, and shadow-band colors can be set directly. A Rim Shade Color blend opacity of 0 preserves the existing 1st Shadow Color. Output Master Saturation — Applies to the final output: 0 is grayscale, 1 is the baseline, and values above 1 strengthen chroma while preserving brightness. Per-layer UV selection — Choose UV Source (UV0–UV3) independently for each normal layer and Mask UV Source separately for its mask. With both at UV0 (the default), the UV-router variant is not compiled.

Language display — Installation and update messages select Korean, Japanese, or English for other system languages; Manager labels continue to follow the Inspector language selection. Conversion output — Converted materials retain emission-map RGB/alpha and emission-mask RGBA data, including surface-alpha blending for transparent materials. Per-layer normal UV Source and mask Mask UV Source (UV0–UV3) choices are copied as well.

Shader baking — Identical requests are grouped to reduce duplicate work during repeated bakes while preserving existing generated output and state. Generated-output recovery — Interrupted bakes now recover without leaving partial files that can poison the next generated-shader cache. Outline normal stability — Replaced the outline normal's object-scale-sensitive geometric correction with finite, scale-invariant handling and an authored-direction fallback for degenerate or non-finite geometry.
Manager Notes opens the latest localized documentation, while the current and latest versions remain visible together.

Back up your project, then move any personal materials, textures, or presets out of Assets/StudioRaming/MingToon. For an older Assets-based installation, delete only that MingToon folder before importing the new installer. Do not delete MingLightController or the entire StudioRaming folder. This cleanup is only for migration from the older installation method, not for every subsequent VPM update.

By the end of this guide you will create one MingToon material, apply it to a model, and visually confirm that toon shading is actually enabled. Takes about 5 minutes. This guide covers one material. If you want to migrate a whole avatar at once, go to lilToon Conversion.

In the Project panel, right-click → Create > Material. Select the created material and open the shader dropdown at the top of the Inspector. Select StudioRaming > MingToon > BRP. This is correct. The Inspector changes from the generic Standard shader UI to the MingToon-specific inspector. Material is pink? The shader did not compile. Most commonly the render pipeline does not match, or the build target does not satisfy shader model 4.5. → Troubleshooting

Set the surface mode before adding a base map. Changing it later shifts the render queue, causing depth-based effects to turn off entirely. Part Surface Mode Body, clothing Opaque Hair, eyelashes Cutout (Alpha Cutoff 0.3~0.6) Translucent and needs depth effect Transparent · Outline Depth Ready See details in Basics.

Confirm the Inspector view mode is Simple. Add your character texture to the Base Map slot. Drag the material onto the model's Renderer to apply it. This is correct. The character appears in the scene with texture color, and sharp-edged shadows form based on light direction. This sharp boundary is the signal that toon shading is on. If you see only soft gradients, the shader is still Standard.

In Simple mode, adjusting only these changes the look significantly. Item What it does When first tuning Base Map HSVG Hue/Saturation/Value/Gamma correction of base color Adjust tone without changing the original texture 1st Shadow Softness (Quick Look) Edge softness width of the shadow boundary Tune this first. 0.001 = cell, 0.3+ = gradient Base Color Preservation How much of the original color to keep even in darkness High for VRChat world variance Minimum Final Brightness Never go darker than this Prevents characters disappearing in dark worlds Especially important in VRChat World lighting is beyond the avatar creator's control. Raising Base Color Preservation and Minimum Final Brightness ensures your character survives any world. → Light & Shadow

Switch the view mode to Full. In the Outline group's Normal Outline section, enable Enable Classic Hull. Adjust Outline Width and Outline Color. (Also available in Quick Look) This is correct. A line appears around the character silhouette. Normal outline does not need camera depth, so it works everywhere. In contrast, Inner 2D Edge for drawing inner lines like clothing wrinkles reads the camera depth texture, requiring separate setup.
